title: Optically induced flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene
extended_summary:
This paper addresses whether flat electronic bands, normally accessible only near the magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene, can be created and controlled using light. The authors ask if coherent optical driving can flatten bands, open spectral gaps, and potentially induce topological properties in small-angle twisted bilayer graphene where undriven bands are not sufficiently flat or isolated.

The intervention studied is not an educational intervention but a theoretical Floquet-engineering scheme: a circularly polarized optical field is applied to a continuum model of twisted bilayer graphene. The authors analyze the resulting Floquet band structure under different twist angles, driving frequencies, field strengths, and lattice-relaxation parameters, using numerical calculations of quasi-energy spectra, time-averaged density of states, and Chern numbers.

The paper considers low-angle twisted bilayer graphene and shows that sufficiently strong but still sub-bandwidth light in the visible to near-infrared range can open gaps between the upper and lower bands near charge neutrality, isolate them from remote bands, and reduce their bandwidth. These effects are reported to be robust to realistic lattice relaxation and to persist over a wide range of twist angles below the magic angle. The authors also find that, in an off-resonant regime, the driven system can acquire nonzero Chern numbers for the flat bands, suggesting the possibility of topological flat-band states.
